articles.content: A Pakistani man has been sentenced to 27 1/2 years in federal prison for his role in an Iran-backed plot to kill President Trump and former President Joe Biden. The man, Asif Merchant, was convicted of attempted terrorism and orchestrating a murder-for-hire scheme at the direction of Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps. Asif Merchant appeared in court with a solemn expression, shackled ankles visible beneath his tan prison attire as he took in his surroundings. His wavy gray hair stood out against the drabness of the courtroom, where he faced up to life in prison for his crimes. District Judge Eric R. Komitee presided over the sentencing hearing, his wavy gray hair standing out against the drab courtroom backdrop. The judge noted that Iran's involvement in the plot was a significant factor in determining the severity of the sentence. As he spoke, it became clear that the Iranian government's influence had been instrumental in orchestrating the assassination attempt. Merchant's role in the plot involved recruiting associates and hiring hit men to carry out the scheme, which also included stealing documents from the target's home and arranging a protest as a diversion after the murder occurred. According to court documents, the plan was elaborate and multifaceted, with several components designed to maximize its chances of success. During his own testimony, Merchant admitted that he had been recruited by a member of Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps, an elite military branch that answers directly to the supreme leader. His admission provided further evidence of the Iranian government's direct involvement in the plot, and served as a stark reminder of the country's reputation as a major sponsor of terrorism worldwide. The trial of a man convicted in an Iranian-backed plot to kill a high-profile US government official has taken another turn. A key aspect of the case involved a potential target who turned out to be a confidential source working with law enforcement. Merchant's alleged accomplices were actually undercover FBI agents, and he claimed on the stand that he carried out the plot under duress, fearing harm to his family in Iran if he didn't comply. Iran has vehemently denied any involvement in a plot to harm Mr. S., a senior government official, despite evidence presented by prosecutors. The country's authorities have highlighted Merchant's own online posts as proof of his intentions, specifically mentioning a post featuring an image of Mr. S. Trial records show that Merchant had been researching locations for Trump campaign rallies in 2024 and even looked up the address of at least one event on Google Maps. To conceal their true purpose, Merchant set up a clothing business, using coded language related to garments to discuss the plot with co-conspirators. However, during sentencing, Merchant's lawyer Christopher Neff argued that the garment business was genuine, rather than a front for illicit activities. The court delivered a guilty verdict in the case against Merchant, who had been accused of being part of an Iran-backed plot to assassinate former President Trump. However, during sentencing, his lawyer argued that the garment business was genuine and not a front for illicit activities. Merchant's defense team maintained he was innocent, claiming he was being unfairly portrayed as a monster by the government. The court ultimately delivered its verdict, but details of the sentence were not immediately disclosed, leaving behind a complex web of intrigue surrounding the case. articles.title: Nvidia Chairperson Harvey Jones Confirms No Return for Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia's chairperson Harvey Jones closed the door on speculation about Jensen Huang's potential return to the company during its first earnings call without him at the helm.
articles.content: Nvidia's chairperson Harvey Jones closed the door on speculation about Jensen Huang's potential return to the company during its first earnings call without him at the helm. The board of directors has made it clear that they do not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO, with Jones stating that "we will not be addressing or taking questions on today's call regarding the circumstances of Jensen's resignation and the ongoing investigation". This ruling out of discussion about why Huang left has been met with a lack of inquiry from analysts, with none of the eight present on the call asking follow-up questions. The absence of questions about Huang's departure and subsequent investigation was notable, given that Nvidia had just reported a significant beating of Wall Street estimates in quarterly revenue. The company posted $115.8 billion in revenue, a staggering figure that saw its stock rise nearly 5% in after-hours trading to around $163 per share. Jones provided some insight into Huang's resignation during the call, stating that he "voluntarily resigned on November 12 due to personal behavior that was inconsistent with Nvidia's code of conduct and cultural norms. The board accepted his resignation unanimously, Jones noted, adding that they have since hired a search firm to consider both internal and external candidates for the top role. The call with analysts had a one-question limit, but Bank of America's Vivek Arya managed to squeeze in a question about talent retention and leadership transition. Interim CEO Colette Kress responded that among employees, there is a mix of opinions on the situation. From a business perspective, it appears that everything is proceeding as usual, according to Kress. Analysts also asked about margins, vendor financing, and next year's outlook during the call. Their questions were focused on the company's financial health and future prospects. However, one question was noticeably absent from the discussion: the issue of customers billed in Singapore. According to Nvidia's 10-Q filing, $10.2 billion in sales, representing 22% of its revenue, came from these customers in the quarter that ended July 2025. It is worth noting that the majority of this revenue, over 99%, was attributed to orders from U.S.-based customers. The company explained in its filing that customers use Singapore for centralized invoicing purposes, while their products are often shipped elsewhere. The discrepancy between the billing location and the actual shipping destination raises questions about the nature of these transactions and how they fit into Nvidia's business operations. Nvidia's shift to reporting revenue by customer headquarters location has eliminated Singapore as a separate line item, providing a new perspective on its geographic revenue profile. A criminal investigation into Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company, is being led jointly by the Commerce and Justice departments, which had begun probing the firm in 2024. The investigation centers around allegations that Megaspeed helped Nvidia export high-end technology to China. According to reports, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on a no sell" list in June 2025. The Wall Street Journal has revealed that the Securities and Exchange Commission is launching a separate civil probe into whether Nvidia's disclosures have been misleading investors. This development adds another layer of scrutiny for the company as it navigates the complex landscape surrounding its business dealings with China. Nvidia has announced that licensed Hopper data center chip sales to China generated $2.4 billion in revenue during the last quarter, but the company is no longer shipping these products to the country. The firm's forecast for the next quarter assumes zero data center compute revenue from China, indicating a significant shift in its business strategy. Nvidia's chairwoman has emphasized that the company will carefully examine new export rules from the Commerce Department, which impose stricter controls on access to advanced chips via other countries. The firm is poised to maintain strong performance due to an ongoing mismatch between demand and supply, despite these increased regulatory hurdles. Meanwhile, Nvidia has upgraded its revenue growth forecast for fiscal 2028 to around 75%, up from a previous estimate of 70%. This revised projection suggests the company remains confident in its prospects despite the challenging export environment. Nvidia's customer base is also undergoing significant changes, with frontier AI labs expected to account for approximately 15% of the company's data center revenue this year. The firm will soon release its first regional revenue breakdown since Jensen Huang's exit as CEO, which is scheduled to be included in its upcoming 10-Q filing. As part of ongoing investigations, Huang and general counsel Tim Teter have agreed to provide transcribed interviews with three House committees. His take on Batman was a critical and commercial success, praised for its dark and atmospheric tone, which drew comparisons to David Fincher's Se7en. The film's influence can still be felt in the ongoing debate over the future of the franchise. The same risk-averse approach is likely to prevail with Bond, given the high stakes involved. This would mean revisiting familiar themes and tropes, rather than pushing the boundaries of the character. The challenge of revamping the James Bond franchise lies in finding a balance between its nostalgic roots and modern innovation. With Pattinson at the helm, it's possible to envision a Bond who is not just a brooding figure but also someone with a playful edge. In fact, giving camp a chance could be the key to making this new iteration of Bond truly stand out from its predecessors. By embracing a more relaxed and humorous approach, Villeneuve and Pattinson can create a character that's both faithful to the original while still feeling distinctly modern. articles.title: Nationwide Ground Stop Causes Disruptions and Delays in US Air Travel
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration's request for $50 billion in new funding has been met with skepticism from lawmakers, who question whether such a large sum is justified.
articles.content: Air travel in the US has been severely disrupted following a nationwide ground stop that caused widespread delays and cancellations for thousands of flights on Friday. The Federal Aviation Administration is seeking $50 billion in new funding to address the crisis, a significant increase from its initial request of $30 billion. The sudden surge in funding demand was outlined in a letter signed by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who has been criticized for his handling of the situation. Despite calls for accountability, Duffy has refused to apologize or accept responsibility for the failure, instead blaming predecessors and Congress. He has publicly rebuked Congress for its role in the crisis. In a closed-door briefing with Senate Republicans on Tuesday, Duffy faced intense questioning from multiple senators who "yelled at him during the meeting, according to an individual present but not authorized to speak publicly about the discussion. The tension was palpable as Senate Republican leaders and Duffy opted to hold separate news conferences after the briefing. A $50 billion price tag for fixing air travel issues has sparked heated debate on Capitol Hill, with some lawmakers questioning whether such a large sum is justified. The proposal, put forth by Rep. Sean Duffy, was met with skepticism and frustration from Democrats who felt he failed to provide sufficient justification for the massive funding request. Duffy's decision to meet only with Republican colleagues on Tuesday has added fuel to the fire, with many arguing that bipartisan support is essential in addressing such a critical issue. The regular government funding process requires cooperation from both parties, yet Duffy chose not to involve Democrats in his initial discussions. Democrats are now calling for a more detailed explanation of how the proposed funds would be allocated and what specific upgrades they would cover. Some have expressed concern that the $12 billion already allocated for air traffic control has yet to be fully utilized, making it unclear why an additional $50 billion is necessary. Senator Brian Schatz of Hawaii is closely watching the air travel funding debate as he prepares to take on a key leadership role in the Senate. As majority whip and a member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Schatz will be instrumental in shaping the final bill. The looming deadline of December 11 adds an extra layer of urgency to the negotiations. If Congress fails to reach a deal by then, it could trigger another government shutdown, which would have far-reaching consequences for various sectors. Lawmakers are now weighing their options on how to proceed with funding the government. One possibility is that Republicans might push through a party-line reconciliation" bill to approve military funding without needing Democratic support. However, Democrats are unlikely to agree to additional military funds unless there's progress on ending the war in Iran. Sean Duffy's proposal to allocate $50 billion to address air travel issues was met with skepticism in Congress on Tuesday. He expressed his willingness to work with Democrats to pass the funds, but chose to meet exclusively with Republicans. Duffy emphasized that he has a good relationship with Democratic lawmakers and has spent considerable time discussing the issue with them over the phone. When asked by reporters about his decision to only meet with Republicans, he noted that he is not trying to dictate how Democrats conduct their work. articles.title: Trends in Travel Highlight Shift Towards Immersive Culinary Experiences
articles.summary: A series of expert-led discussions shed light on the latest trends in immersive culinary experiences and multigenerational travel.
articles.content: Our Points of View Summit kicked off with a series of expert-led discussions that shed light on the latest trends in travel. The event featured an array of panels and breakouts where our team of specialists shared their insights on various topics. Travelers are increasingly seeking out immersive culinary experiences, and our summit provided a platform for experts to share their knowledge on this subject. Senior features editor Megan Spurrell and editorial assistant Skyli Alvarez led a discussion on the evolution of food travel, from traditional cooking classes to more adventurous pursuits like foraging. The interest in authentic food moments is clear, but defining what constitutes authenticity can be a challenge. According to Omolola Campbell, executive producer of The Spirit We Move With, an intimate understanding of local culture and traditions is essential to creating meaningful culinary experiences. Campbell shared the significance of okra in Gullah cuisine, explaining that its use in traditional dishes is deeply rooted in the history of West African slaves who were brought to South Carolina. "Taking a cooking class is much different than getting it from a local chef," she said, highlighting the importance of stories and context in understanding the cultural significance of food. The summit also explored the changing dynamics of multigenerational travel, with our specialists discussing the ways in which families are choosing to spend their vacations together. The rise of all-inclusive stays has been particularly notable in recent years, offering a convenient and stress-free option for travelers seeking a hassle-free getaway. As we continue to explore the latest trends in travel, one thing is clear: today's travelers crave experiences that go beyond mere sightseeing. They seek out immersive, authentic moments that allow them to connect with local cultures and traditions. Travelers today are seeking unique experiences that allow them to connect with local cultures and traditions in an authentic way. The traditional notion of multigenerational travel is evolving as grandparents join trips at older ages, often alongside younger family members who choose the destinations. This shift has significant implications for trip designers, who must now cater to a wide range of activity levels and exertion needs within one itinerary. To accommodate this diverse group, it's recommended that families have multiple options available on any given day, allowing younger travelers to pursue their interests while still coming together for shared experiences. Mealtimes and afternoon activities are ideal opportunities for family members to reunite, and boat and yacht experiences can be particularly beneficial in fostering a sense of togetherness among family members. The luxury travel industry's definition of opulence is undergoing a significant shift, according to experts who gathered at our recent summit. Luxury, Virgi Schiffino Kennedy, managing partner at Lux Voyage, explained, "is being able to pass on meaning to kids [and] exposing families to the broader world and its cultures," highlighting its intangible appeal. This perspective emphasizes the importance of creating lasting memories and experiences for future generations. A key demographic driving this shift is Gen Z and Millennials, who are more inclined to spend on travel but want transparency about where their money goes, Thomas Robinson, MR at Dehouche, noted. As a result, travelers are seeking authentic and immersive experiences that align with their values. The trend of family members traveling together is also evolving, with 30- and 40-somethings increasingly treating their parents to vacations, rather than the other way around. Milestone birthdays and anniversaries are driving clients to book trips, according to Harnal's experience. As the Euro summer season approaches, concerns about overtourism, price inflation, and rising temperatures are top of mind for travelers. Director of special projects Lale Arikoglu and commerce editor Meaghan Kenny opened the floor for our specialists to weigh in on these pressing issues. Some experts recommend exploring Switzerland as an alternative to popular destinations like the Dolomites, where crowds can be overwhelming. Brian Dore, owner of CIU Travel, suggested considering one-day hiking trails or "soft adventure travel in Switzerland, combining a lake or city destination with outdoor activities for three-to-four days. For families looking for a unique experience, destinations like Umbria in Italy offer an abundance of festivals and craft activities perfect for kids to enjoy. Alternatively, Austria, Ireland, or Croatia provide excellent options for those seeking a mix of culture and outdoor adventure. Traveling during the shoulder season can be beneficial, as May is now being recommended over August for those who prefer milder weather on their European vacations. When planning a trip to France, flying into Paris or Nice allows visitors to easily explore the countryside or lesser-known Atlantic Coast regions. Before embarking on any journey, it's essential to check the local climate conditions in advance to ensure a comfortable and enjoyable experience. The demand for travel to Asia continues to rise, with Mei Zhang, chairman and founder at WildChina, highlighting the increasing popularity of destinations across the continent. As the travel industry continues to evolve, sporting events, music festivals, and art fairs are becoming major draws for travelers. These high-demand events often require bundled purchases due to limited availability of individual tickets, as seen at Pink's performance at The Sphere, which necessitates a Venetian hotel package. The lack of stringent legal protections in the US enables extreme ticket scalping for stadium concerts, making domestic events increasingly unaffordable for many. This has created a challenge for travel advisors like Stephanie Malakie, founder of Empress Travel Club, who struggle to filter options and find suitable experiences for clients amidst the numerous events and providers. To navigate this issue, specialists recommend curating the surrounding experience or tapping into niche experiential travel opportunities, such as watching sports teams play in unique locations like London's Wembley Stadium. Cultural milestones like attending European Christmas markets or Vatican City trips featuring Papal Blessings can also be paired with entertainment options for a more immersive experience. Set-jetting to filming locations is another trend gaining traction, offering value without the hassle of peak-event ticketing, according to Mei Zhang's observations. This approach allows travelers to explore new destinations and tap into their interests in a more relaxed manner. The great outdoors has become a major focus in travel, with many seeking nature-based wellness experiences. However, experts warn that the trend for dumbphone fantasies", disconnecting from technology and immersing oneself in natural settings, may be less achievable than anticipated due to logistical challenges and limited availability of such experiences. Guests at the Points of View Summit are looking for a balance between technology access and natural immersion, but not necessarily a complete digital detox. According to Kate Doty, trip designer at Geographic Expeditions, Wi-Fi is still a must-have for emergency purposes, with no guest requesting a full digital detox. This suggests that while travelers want to disconnect from the digital world, they also value having some level of connectivity available. To reduce dependency on phones, services like on-board photographers can be offered, allowing guests to capture memories without needing their own devices. The trend towards glamping is also still strong, with travelers seeking luxury and nature in equal measure. This desire for both comfort and immersion is driving the demand for unique experiences that combine these two elements. By reframing a destination's seasons and characteristics, it's possible to find value in what might otherwise be seen as drawbacks. For example, a rainy season can bring lush greenery and other benefits that make a trip more enjoyable. By embracing this unpredictability and incorporating it into travel plans, travelers can have a more authentic and engaging experience, learning something new with each visit. articles.title: Breakthrough in Supercomputer Workflow Accelerates Protein Structure Prediction
articles.summary: Researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory have developed an optimized computing workflow that enables the generation of predicted protein structures at an unprecedented rate.
articles.content: A breakthrough in supercomputer workflow has enabled researchers to accelerate the generation of predicted protein structures at an unprecedented rate. This achievement, led by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), promises to revolutionize various fields including drug discovery and biological research. The optimized computing workflow is part of a project called ElMerFold, which leverages advanced biomolecular models for improved accuracy. By generating millions of predicted protein structures as training data, the team aims to enhance these models' capabilities. Researchers from LLNL collaborated with experts at AMD and Columbia University to push the limits of high-performance computing on El Capitan, a machine capable of exascale operations. The result was astonishing: over 10,700 predicted protein structures per second were generated across thousands of accelerated processing units. The team's achievement has earned them a spot among finalists for the prestigious ACM Gordon Bell Prize, with the winner to be announced next month at the SC26 conference in Chicago. The project's scope extended beyond the realm of protein folding, as it aimed to develop new capabilities for large-scale superintelligence research and infrastructure. According to Brian Van Essen, this collaboration offered a unique chance to tackle pressing challenges in biology and machine learning workflows for high-performance computing. Proteins play a crucial role in nearly every biological process, and understanding their three-dimensional structures is essential for determining how they function and interact with other molecules. The experimental determination of protein structures is often expensive and time-consuming, limiting the amount of available data for developing computational prediction models. Researchers acknowledge that this shortage of real data hinders the training of state-of-the-art protein structure prediction models. Nikoli Dryden notes that acquiring new experimental structures requires significant resources in terms of time, expense, and effort. As a result, researchers must supplement these limited data with synthetic information to aid their predictions. Existing prediction models are generating synthetic protein structures to train new models in a process called distillation. This approach is crucial for producing large data sets required by modern biomolecular models, which can be computationally expensive and sometimes costlier than the models themselves. The resulting data set is being used to enhance OpenFold3's ability to predict complex molecular interactions, particularly those between antibodies and antigens they recognize. According to Mohammed AlQuraishi, a collaborator on the ElMerFold project, this distillation set improves OpenFold3 performance by refining its understanding of protein structure biophysics. Understanding how antibodies bind to biological targets is essential for developing therapeutics against infectious diseases, and predicting drug-protein interactions could accelerate early-stage drug discovery. To achieve the desired performance level, the research team had to thoroughly optimize both the prediction software and the underlying computing infrastructure. This involved leveraging the capabilities of El Capitan's processors by scaling the workflow across nearly its entire system. The researchers exploited the unique features of AMD's MI300A APUs, which integrate CPUs and GPUs with shared high-bandwidth memory, thereby reducing unnecessary data transfers and enhancing computational efficiency. By doing so, they were able to streamline the computing process and minimize delays. Specialized components were developed to fine-tune El Capitan's processors, including optimized computational kernels, advanced memory management strategies, and innovative scheduling techniques. This allowed the system to operate at peak performance levels without compromising its processing capacity. To further enhance efficiency, the team implemented persistent inference servers, eliminating the need for repeated model loading, and utilized El Capitan's Rabbit near-node storage system from HPE for rapid data access. Throughout this optimization process, the researchers collaborated closely with Columbia University experts in protein folding to ensure that performance gains did not come at the expense of prediction accuracy. The team also made significant contributions to compiler frameworks such as DaCe, enabling the generation of highly optimized computations tailored to the MI300A architecture. This expertise could potentially benefit other applications and programs within the lab, as expressed by LLNL computer scientist Tal Ben-Nun: "We went as far as writing machine-level instructions to maximize the performance of the system." The optimization of ElMerFold has led to significant advancements in protein-structure prediction, thanks to its ability to harness the power of El Capitan's AMD Instinct MI300A architecture and AMD ROCm software. This achievement is particularly noteworthy given the importance of exascale systems in accelerating the creation of training data for scientific models. As a result, researchers can now generate larger and more detailed datasets, opening up new avenues of inquiry across various disciplines such as materials science, chemistry, and physics. The implications of ElMerFold extend beyond molecular biology to LLNL's national security mission, where limited training data poses a significant challenge. This scarcity of data hinders the development of computational models for stockpile modernization and other applications in the NNSA mission space. To address this challenge, researchers are exploring the use of scientifically grounded synthetic training data, which ElMerFold has shown to be an effective approach. By doing so, scientists can better interpret and understand rare or anomalous events, a crucial aspect of their work in national security missions. The ElMerFold data set has been made accessible to researchers worldwide, enabling them to create new scientific models using the predictions. This move is expected to foster further development of protein-structure prediction methods. To enhance its capabilities, the team aims to generate a wider range of training data sets, including those for predicting complex proteins composed of multiple interacting molecules. The inclusion of these diverse datasets will provide researchers with more robust tools for their work. The researchers plan to integrate the latest OpenFold3 model into the ElMerFold workflow, ultimately refining the core scalable inference framework to make it adaptable to various scientific workloads. articles.title: Nvidia Quarterly Earnings Report Set for Release
articles.summary: The chipmaker is set to release its quarterly earnings report on Tuesday, providing a glimpse into its financial health after a tumultuous period.
articles.content: Nvidia's quarterly earnings report is set to be released on Tuesday, providing a glimpse into the company's financial health after a tumultuous period. The chipmaker has seen its stock price plummet 35% from its peak last month, wiping out nearly $2 trillion in market value and sparking widespread concern among investors. The AI industry, which Nvidia is at the forefront of, is now under scrutiny as the company struggles to reassure investors. If Nvidia fails to deliver a convincing earnings report, it could have far-reaching consequences for the entire sector, potentially dragging other companies down with it. The stakes are high, and investors are anxiously waiting for news. Jensen Huang's sudden departure from the CEO position has left a power vacuum at Nvidia, which he founded. In a statement, Huang pledged to return as CEO if the board of directors deemed it in the best interest of shareholders and the country. However, despite calls from influential figures including President Donald Trump, the board has yet to make a decision. The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia over allegations that the company misled investors. This probe adds to the growing list of concerns surrounding the chipmaker's financials and business practices. The investigation is also fueling fears about potential national security implications arising from Nvidia's involvement in illegal export deals. Colette Kress, Nvidia's finance chief and interim CEO, will be under intense scrutiny as she attempts to convince investors that the company is on a stable trajectory. Market confidence has been shaken by supply chain backlogs for advanced chips and servers, which are critical components of AI infrastructure and large language models. Nvidia's strategic maneuvering under Huang has made it a crucial player for AI labs and data centers, not just by supplying hardware but also by providing financial backing through various means. Critics have raised concerns that Nvidia's circular financing schemes, which involve funding hyperscalers like Meta or Microsoft in exchange for product purchases, may have contributed to the inflated AI bubble. These arrangements have been a source of contention among executives, including Kress. Nvidia is reportedly reassessing its involvement in high-risk AI financial deals, such as investments in OpenAI and infrastructure companies like Lambda. This shift comes after scaling back financing for a $250 billion OpenAI data center deal, which was a significant undertaking. The tech industry may face challenges if Nvidia continues to distance itself from GPU commitments. The semiconductor production landscape is highly specialized, dominated by a few key players, making supply chain disruptions potentially far-reaching and affecting consumer electronics and cloud services. Nvidia's handling of outstanding deals inked under Huang's leadership will be closely watched during the earnings call, particularly since the company can no longer rely on revenue from certain export arrangements. Nvidia's dominance in the market for data center hardware and AI model training has led to a situation where demand far outstrips supply. The shortage of RAM and high-bandwidth memory is particularly problematic as it slows down production and drives up costs for cloud companies and other buyers. To mitigate this issue, Nvidia has invested heavily in securing future memory supplies, but the effort may not be enough to alleviate the bottleneck. Meanwhile, the controversy surrounding Huang's personal life has created new challenges for the company. His ties to a Chinese executive linked to Megaspeed have raised questions about the integrity of the supply chain. The company's reliance on third-party countries to divert advanced chips to China has been identified as a significant issue by investment research firm Culper, which estimates that up to one-fifth of Nvidia's compute revenues in fiscal year 2026 came from this process. The AI buildout relies heavily on hardware companies like Nvidia, making them vulnerable to industry-wide downturns in investor confidence. If Nvidia's earnings call indicates strong growth, it could boost stocks and funds focused on technology, potentially leading to a surge in the value of individual retirement accounts and 401(k)s. Major funds and indices are dominated by a handful of big tech companies, often referred to as the Magnificent Seven. These firms account for nearly one-third of the S&P 500 index and have significant exposure to AI-related stocks. This means that investors who hold these companies through index funds may be indirectly affected by fluctuations in Nvidia's stock price. The impact of an AI selloff could extend beyond individual investors, potentially affecting retirement balances even for those who don't own Nvidia shares directly. The Magnificent Seven are particularly vulnerable to AI stock swings, with their share prices often closely tied to the performance of companies like OpenAI and Anthropic. Alphabet's recent experience serves as a stark reminder that even top tech firms can be affected by market fluctuations triggered by Nvidia news. Intel and CoreWeave, both heavily focused on AI infrastructure, have also seen their share prices decline in response to growing concerns over AI dangers. As the debate around AI risks intensifies, companies like Nvidia are facing increased scrutiny over their role in the development of artificial general intelligence. The company's CEO has been a prominent advocate for AI, framing it as an economic and national-security imperative, but recent developments have raised questions about the pace and scope of AI advancements. The recent controversies surrounding Huang's leadership have added to the growing unease about the pace and scope of AI advancements in the US. As Nvidia prepares for its earnings call, the tech industry is bracing itself for a potential backlash against data centers and large-scale AI projects, which have become increasingly unpopular among politicians and voters. Democrats are pushing for stricter regulations on the AI industry, including laws to prevent an industry bailout if a bubble were to burst. This shift in public opinion has caught many in the industry off guard. The bipartisan calls for Huang to testify before Congress have highlighted concerns about Nvidia's dealings with China and potential export loopholes. Some politicians are also investigating high-ranking officials at US intelligence and the Commerce Department, accusing them of failing to act on knowledge of Nvidia's China-related deals. This scrutiny is likely to continue in the coming months. Kress may be able to distance herself from some of Nvidia's riskiest ventures, but her predecessor's relationships have left a lasting impact on the company's national security implications. The investigation into these dealings has opened up a Pandora's box that no CEO can easily close. The federal government's response to these developments is likely to be slow and cumbersome, but there is an increasing momentum towards investigating the major players in the AI industry. This will undoubtedly have a chilling effect on investor hype and put pressure on companies like Nvidia to re-evaluate their priorities. articles.title: Groundbreaking Breakthrough in Chemical Manufacturing Using Electricity
articles.summary: Researchers from Harvard University have successfully demonstrated that essential medicines and fine chemicals can be produced using electricity instead of hazardous processes.
articles.content: A groundbreaking breakthrough in chemical manufacturing has been achieved by a team of researchers from Harvard University. They have successfully demonstrated that essential medicines and fine chemicals can be produced using electricity instead of hazardous processes involving intense heat and heavy-metal catalysts. The new study published in Nature Catalysis presents an innovative metal-free electrosynthetic strategy that repurposes water-soluble organic battery materials as chemical shuttles. This approach has the potential to revolutionize the production of critical chemicals, reducing the reliance on polluting processes. The research was led by Richard Liu and Michael Aziz, in collaboration with Joonho Lee and other Harvard researchers. They have explored an alternative method for nitro reduction, a common transformation used in chemical manufacturing, which is foundational for producing active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals, dyes, and more. Nitro groups are often converted into primary amines through industrial processes that emit significant amounts of carbon dioxide equivalent per kilogram of hydrogen. These methods also rely on single-use reducing agents that generate substantial waste. The new research aims to address these issues by providing a cleaner alternative for nitro reduction. The conventional approach to organic electrosynthesis faces a significant challenge: water is excellent at conducting electricity, but it struggles to dissolve organic compounds, while organic solvents are adept at dissolving reactants but poor at transmitting electrical currents. Researchers have discovered that ultrastable and water-soluble phenazines can facilitate the transfer of electrons and protons across a liquid-liquid interface under mild conditions. These phenazines were originally developed for use in grid-scale flow batteries, where they demonstrated remarkable stability. The idea is to harness the properties of these molecules to address a major hurdle in organic electrosynthesis: "A lot of people doing organic electrochemistry are trying to pass these currents through relatively nonconductive organic solvents," notes Liu. By leveraging the design principles developed for flow battery electrolytes, it may be possible to enable more efficient and effective chemical reactions. The research team's recognition that the rules governing battery engineering can inform solutions in organic chemistry has been a key breakthrough. As Alfaraidi points out, "Battery engineering and organic chemistry, these two fields do not really normally talk to each other very much," but their collaboration has yielded promising results. The team's experimental setup involved placing phenazines in a saltwater solution inside an electrochemical cell, where they were charged with protons and electrons through electrical stimulation. This process created a two-phase mixture when the solution was pumped into a reactor alongside an organic solvent containing the target substrate, allowing for chemical reactions to occur at the interface between the two phases. At this interface, the phenazine molecules transferred their charges to the substrate via proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), before returning to the water phase to be recharged with new protons and electrons. The researchers have successfully designed a method that enables each side of the reaction - electrochemistry and organic chemistry - to operate in its preferred environment, while still allowing them to communicate chemically. By using phenazine molecules as shuttles, the team demonstrated high efficiency and precision in converting challenging chemical compounds, unlike traditional catalysts that can destroy sensitive functional groups such as double bonds or halogen rings. The reaction mixture separates into two distinct streams as it flows over internal barriers, one of which can be recycled back into the cell. To gain a deeper understanding of how chemical reactions occur at interfaces, researchers combined kinetic analysis, surface science, and quantum chemical modeling to study the boundary between oil and water. Their findings confirmed that proton and electron motion are closely linked during the rate-determining step. This insight is crucial for optimizing reaction efficiency. The team conducted further experiments to determine what drives the reaction rates in this system. They discovered that it's not the shuttle's ability to reduce chemical compounds, but rather its affinity for the oil-water interface that determines how quickly reactions occur. The shuttle's density of adsorption at the interface is a key factor. From an engineering perspective, researchers considered whether the mediator could withstand repeated use and maintain its effectiveness over time. This is essential for determining the overall viability of the process, as chemical mediators can be expensive to replace if they degrade too quickly. The team has successfully built a continuous-flow system that achieves a high yield of 91%. The economic feasibility of this process depends heavily on the cost and durability of the mediator used. The innovative research project has reached a significant milestone, with the discovery of repurposed battery molecules driving key chemical reactions at an oil-water interface. articles.content: The Bon Appétit Test Kitchen in New York City opened its doors to the public for an immersive day of cooking experiences and classes. The event, called Bon Appétit Live, featured a packed schedule of activities that catered to both beginners and seasoned cooks. In addition to hands-on classes and demonstrations, attendees could also explore the Test Kitchen's archives through a new cooking app launched by the publication. The new app contains tens of thousands of recipes from the Test Kitchen's extensive collection. According to sources within the company, this digital resource is designed to provide users with access to a vast library of culinary knowledge. With its comprehensive database and intuitive interface, the app aims to make cooking easier and more enjoyable for everyone. In one of the day's first classes, Pie Crust Fundamentals, attendees learned the basics of making perfect pie crusts from Senior Test Kitchen Editor Jesse Szewczyk. This interactive class was presented by East Fork, a ceramics brand that has collaborated with Bon Appétit on several projects. Participants were able to put their newfound skills into practice at designated stations throughout the kitchen. Szewczyk and his guest instructor, Keia Mastrianni, guided attendees through the process of making a buttery pie crust fortified with cream cheese. This recipe, developed by former Senior Test Kitchen Editor Shilpa Uskokovic, is particularly well-suited for special occasions like Thanksgiving. As participants worked on their pie dough, Test Kitchen editors were on hand to offer expert guidance and answer any questions. Mastrianni, who has earned the nickname "unofficial pie lady of East Fork, was enthusiastic about sharing her passion for pie making with the audience. When asked about her love of pies, she exclaimed: I love preaching the gospel of pie. The attendees of Bon Appétit LIVE left with more than just new pie-making skills, they also received a ceramic pie dish from East Fork's new bakeware collection. These dishes are made from clay and glaze sourced in the Southeast, highlighting the brand's commitment to local materials. Emma's and Chris's recipes had clearly been game-changers for many guests, who credited Bon Appétit with making cooking more accessible and building their confidence in the kitchen. The emphasis on practice and honing skills was a recurring theme throughout the event. In the Demo Kitchen, a different kind of culinary expertise was on display as Pasta Boot Camp participants learned from Senior Cooking Editor Kelsey Jane Youngman and chef Stefano Secchi. Secchi's background is impressive, having trained under legendary Italian chef Massimo Bottura in Modena. Secchi's filled ravioli dish, Holiday In Parma, showcased the perfect combination of flavors and textures, 00 flour and egg dough gave way to a chestnut and Parmesan filling, served with a reduction made from chicken broth, butter, and saba. The discussion on Bringing Culture to Cooking panel was led by Editor-in-Chief Jamila Robinson, who facilitated an engaging conversation among three esteemed chefs: Fariyal Abdullahi from Hav & Mar in NYC, Nicholas Bazik from Provenance in Philadelphia, and Vijay Kumar from Semma in NYC. Culture, identity, and personal experience played a significant role in shaping the culinary styles of these talented chefs. Each one drew inspiration from their unique backgrounds and experiences to create innovative dishes that reflect their heritage. Chef Nicholas Bazik introduced his audience to fermented lime juice, a versatile seasoning made by combining fresh lime juice with salt at a specific ratio. This simple yet effective technique allows for endless possibilities in cooking. In contrast, Chef Fariyal Abdullahi enthusiastically championed the use of berbere, an Ethiopian spice blend that she likened to Ethiopian salt due to its ubiquity in the country's cuisine. She emphasized that store-bought blends may not always be of the highest quality and encouraged using fresh ingredients whenever possible. The Test Kitchen hosted a hands-on lobster class with Carly Westerfield from Bon Appétit and Krista Tripp, founder of Aphrodite Oysters in Maine. Participants learned how to break down lobsters and assemble a decadent dip made with cream cheese, mayonnaise, celery, chives, and lemon juice under Westerfield's expert guidance. Each participant received a whole, steamed Maine lobster to work with, along with the necessary ingredients and tools to create their own creamy lobster dip. The demonstration's relaxed atmosphere allowed guests to easily follow along as they watched Chef Conroy prepare the luxurious appetizer. Hard-shell lobsters were used in the demonstration, but Chef Tripp encouraged participants to visit Maine and experience both hard-shell and soft-shell varieties for themselves. Soft-shell lobsters have a sweeter and more tender meat than their hard-shell counterparts, which is typically due to their molting cycle. The molting process causes the lobster's shell to become softer and more pliable, making it easier to crack open and access the meat inside. In Maine, soft-shell lobsters are in season from July through August, a time when they can be harvested for consumption. The cafeteria at the Bon Appétit event was filled with guests eager for the live advice column session, where questions about home cooking and holiday entertaining were put to the test. Bon Appétit Director of Cooking Emma Laperruque presented Chef Amanda Freitag with a series of queries from attendees, one of which stood out: how to handle undercooked turkey legs and thighs each year. The question was a common conundrum for many home cooks, and Freitag had a solution. Freitag recommended removing the legs and cooking them separately, as demonstrated in a BA recipe for Gravy-Braised Turkey. This approach ensured that even the most stubbornly undercooked pieces could be cooked to perfection. In another part of the event space, food stylist Thu Buser was showcasing her exceptional culinary artistry by decorating an elaborate snake cake" with vibrant green swirls and flowers. The stunning display caught the attention of many attendees, who stopped by to admire its intricate design. As guests enjoyed their lunch break, a lively discussion took place between Jamila Robinson and legendary chef Marcus Samuelsson about Back to Green: Rediscovering a World of Delicious, Healthy Eating, their new global plant-forward cookbook co-authored by Robinson. The day's events concluded with a focus on sweet treats as attendees indulged in pastries from Lysée, a boutique pastry shop influenced by Korean and French culture and inspired by New York City. Eunji Lee, winner of North America's Best Pastry Chef Award from The 50, was on hand to meet guests and share her creations. Her pastries showcased the perfect blend of East meets West flavors that have become a hallmark of Lysée's offerings. The wild blueberries used in the day's shortcakes proved to be a hit with attendees, who were impressed by their more saturated color and distinct flavor compared to conventional blueberries. Howard highlighted the unique characteristics of Maine's wild blueberry crop, which is renowned for its exceptional quality. As the day drew to a close, guests left with full bellies and new knowledge about the people and products behind the food they enjoy, thanks in part to the expertise shared by Bon Appétit's culinary personalities and editors. articles.content: Nvidia's sales forecast for its next fiscal year has been significantly increased, reflecting a high level of business confidence following the departure of long-time CEO Jensen Huang. This optimism is evident in the company's recent quarterly results, which exceeded expectations. Interim CEO Colette Kress emphasized on a conference call with analysts that Nvidia's momentum is genuine, pointing to strong demand for its products and ongoing technological advancements within the company. She also highlighted the dedication of Nvidia employees as a key factor driving business success. The robust performance in the latest quarter suggests that Nvidia is well-positioned to continue thriving. Kress made her debut as interim CEO on Tuesday's earnings call, flanked by newly appointed board chair Harvey Jones. Both executives sought to convey a sense of continuity and normalcy within the company, despite Huang's departure. This "business-as-usual approach was underscored by their use of phrases like moving forward." The board has made it clear that it will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, with newly appointed chair Harvey Jones stating this outright at the start of the call. Nvidia has also engaged executive search firm Hedrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement for Huang, who resigned amid controversy over personal relationships. Nvidia's stock surged more than 5% in after-hours trading on Tuesday, marking a significant rebound from its recent decline. The company's fortunes have been closely tied to the performance of its AI-driven business, which has faced growing concerns about its durability despite its impressive growth rates. However, Nvidia's latest move suggests that investors are starting to regain confidence in the company's future prospects. On Tuesday, Nvidia raised its sales expectations for fiscal 2028 year, citing improvements in supply and ongoing strength in demand. This forecast increase is notable, as it exceeds the original guidance provided by Huang himself just three months ago. The revised growth target of 75% now stands in stark contrast to the more modest 70% forecast that had been previously announced. According to Kress, this adjustment reflects the company's ability to adapt and thrive even without its founder at the helm. Analysts are taking note of Nvidia's bold move, with some interpreting it as a statement of confidence in the company's ability to navigate any challenges ahead. Nvidia's latest financial report has revealed a significant surge in revenue, more than doubling from the same period last year and exceeding analyst expectations. The company's net income has seen a substantial increase of 105%, reaching $65.3 billion, with earnings per share coming in at $2.70. As the leading manufacturer of AI chips, Nvidia is projecting a strong fourth quarter, with revenue expected to reach $130 billion, a figure that could potentially exceed analyst predictions by billions of dollars. The company has announced it will submit its official 10-Q report to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in due course, allowing for a slightly delayed filing compared to previous years' earnings announcements. Meanwhile, Nvidia's ties to Megaspeed, a cloud computing firm with alleged connections to Chinese intelligence, have raised concerns about potential export control violations, with the U.S. Department of Justice launching a criminal investigation into the company's practices. Nvidia's confidence in its future prospects remains unwavering despite Jensen Huang's departure from the company. The tech giant has reassessed its sales target for next year, significantly increasing it by tens of billions of dollars. The move follows a period of uncertainty surrounding chip exports, with Nvidia currently evaluating the new regulations. However, Kress emphasized that the company is optimistic about overall demand and its revenue forecast, citing no reason to alter its projections. Nvidia's financial commitments to other companies in the AI industry are also under scrutiny. The company provides billions of dollars in equity investments and financial guarantees to firms like neoclouds building data centers and startups developing AI software. Kress stated that Nvidia will continue to offer support but may not be as generous as it has been in the past, taking a closer look at which companies receive assistance. Nvidia's commitment to supporting the AI ecosystem is likely to remain unchanged despite Jensen Huang's departure from the company. articles.title: Los Angeles Chargers End 11-Game Losing Streak with 23-20 Win Over Baltimore Ravens
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers broke their 11-game losing streak with a narrow win over the Baltimore Ravens, thanks in part to the performance of rookie running back Omarion Hampton.
articles.content: The Los Angeles Chargers have finally broken their 11-game losing streak after a narrow 23-20 win over the Baltimore Ravens. The victory is a much-needed boost for the team, which had been struggling to find its footing on offense. A significant change made by the Chargers during this game was in their running back rotation. They decided to give 2025 first-round pick Omarion Hampton more playing time, and it paid off as he rushed for 105 yards and a touchdown on Monday night. Hampton's performance is notable not only because of his impressive stats but also because it marked one of the biggest workloads of his professional career. The Chargers' win has temporarily lifted the pressure from their shoulders, allowing them to shift focus towards the future. With eight games remaining in the season, they now have a chance to reassess what worked well and what needs improvement as they move forward. The stakes are high for the Chargers, who were on the brink of becoming the first 0-17 team in NFL history before their recent win. Now that this hurdle has been cleared, the team must concentrate on figuring out which players, coaches, and strategies should be retained for next season and what adjustments need to be made during the offseason. The Chargers' offense showed significant improvement on Sunday, allowing quarterback Justin Herbert to breathe a little easier behind center. With a strong ground game taking some of the pressure off, Herbert was able to attempt a season-low 18 passes and still manage to look refreshed and confident. Despite completing just 12 of those passes for 129 yards, Herbert's performance was marked by minimal sacks, only two, and a significant contribution on the ground with 51 yards rushing and a touchdown. Perhaps more importantly, he avoided turning the ball over, giving his team a valuable edge in the turnover margin. The success of the offense can be attributed in part to the hiring of Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator, who has been working to shift the focus away from Herbert's arm and onto other areas of the roster. Unheralded players like Tre Harris have stepped up to fill key roles, with Harris finishing the day with a career-high 86 yards on five receptions. While these developments are certainly encouraging, they do little to address the fundamental questions still plaguing the organization. The lack of game-changing receivers around Herbert remains a major concern, as does the quarterback's ability to adapt to the team's new quick timing offense. And then there's the issue of Rashawn Slater, who has been limited by injuries for much of his career. A winning streak was finally broken after 11 consecutive losses for the Chargers, and it's a much-needed morale boost for the team. The defense played a crucial role in stopping Derrick Henry, who managed just 10 yards on 10 carries - his second-worst output with at least 10 attempts. This is a notable achievement given Henry's Hall of Fame-caliber career. However, the pass defense has shown some weaknesses lately, allowing Jacoby Brissett to throw for 340 yards in his first start for the Ravens and C.J. Straud to rack up 384 yards and five touchdowns in Week 9. Upcoming games against weaker opponents might provide a chance for the Chargers' pass defense to regroup. Running back Scott Matlock played a significant role in the team's success, taking part in a season-high 49.1% of offensive snaps and bringing a physical presence that helped break through defenses. The Chargers' offense showed signs of improvement despite a slow start to their game, which was marked by a fumbled kickoff return by RB Keaton Mitchell early in the second quarter. Luckily for Mitchell, his teammate managed to recover the ball, preventing a potentially costly turnover. Injuries continued to plague the team, with WR Ladd McConkey not traveling with the squad due to a recurring back issue. However, TE Oronde Gadsden II was able to shake off an eye injury and return to action, providing some much-needed stability to the Chargers' receiving corps. The Bolts' struggles on third down were evident, converting just 2 of their 13 attempts for a season-low 15.4%. But they made up for this by successfully executing both of their fourth-down chances, which helped keep their offense moving and gave them a glimmer of hope heading into Sunday's matchup against the Jets. articles.title: Measles-free status lost by US after decades of effort
articles.summary: The United States has lost its measles-free status after decades of concerted efforts to eradicate the highly contagious virus.
articles.content: The United States has lost its measles-free status after decades of concerted efforts to eradicate the highly contagious virus. This reversal is part of a disturbing trend in which vaccination rates are declining globally and locally, allowing once-controlled diseases to resurface and spread rapidly. Measles cases have been on the rise across the Americas since 2024, with multiple countries struggling to contain outbreaks. The US has now joined Mexico and Bolivia as nations where measles elimination efforts have faltered. Mexico's loss of measles-elimination status is a direct result of a significant resurgence of the virus in the country, which culminated in a massive outbreak in Chihuahua state. Bolivia also lost its measles-elimination status after struggling to contain outbreaks across the nation. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has announced that it expects the US, Bolivia, and Mexico to submit plans within weeks on how they will work towards stopping measles transmission for at least a year and regaining their measles elimination status. Measles outbreaks have been spreading across the Americas since 2024, initially affecting close-knit Mennonite communities in North America before expanding to areas with low vaccination rates. Last year, Canada lost its measles-free designation for the first time since 1998, highlighting the growing concern over vaccine-preventable diseases. The measles elimination status is based on whether a single chain of transmission has not occurred within a country's resident population for at least 12 consecutive months. This designation is crucial in assessing a region's public health preparedness and ability to control infectious disease outbreaks. Vaccination rates have been declining globally, including in the US, raising concerns about the resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases like measles. As one of the most contagious diseases known to medicine, measles was seen as a likely candidate to reemerge when vaccination efforts falter. According to Dr. Susan Kansagra, chief medical officer of the Association of State and Territorial Health Officials, measles outbreaks can serve as an early warning sign for other vaccine-preventable diseases. The spread of measles in communities across the United States has become a growing concern due to declining vaccination rates and federal leaders' mixed messages about the importance of getting vaccinated. A significant drop in community vaccination rates below 95% has created an environment where outbreaks can occur, according to experts. The virus is now present in all but three states, with confirmed cases reported throughout the country this year. The past two years have seen a surge in measles cases, with over 7,000 reported and 13 related deaths. The majority of those affected were either not vaccinated or their vaccination status was unknown. Furthermore, nearly 10% of infected individuals required hospitalization for treatment. Measles typically begins with a high fever followed by a distinctive rash that starts on the face before spreading to other areas of the body. Most people recover from the illness, but it remains one of the leading causes of death among young children worldwide according to the World Health Organization. The sudden surge in measles cases across the United States has led to a significant increase in reported illnesses and fatalities. In Texas alone, over 760 people have fallen ill and two children have lost their lives due to the highly contagious disease. Measles outbreaks have also been reported in neighboring states such as New Mexico, Arizona, Utah, and South Carolina. The situation is dire, particularly in rural border towns where access to healthcare services may be limited. In New Mexico, approximately 100 people contracted measles, resulting in one adult fatality. The current outbreak has surpassed all previous ones since 1991, with over 5,400 confirmed cases reported so far this year. This staggering number is already double the total for last year and is largely attributed to a massive outbreak in Pennsylvania. The sheer scale of the epidemic has left public health experts warning that the actual numbers may be significantly higher. The US government's handling of the measles crisis has been criticized by some, particularly given the leadership roles held by individuals with a history of anti-vaccination advocacy. Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the US Health Secretary, was once a vocal proponent of vaccine skepticism before taking on his current role. The struggles with measles in various countries are well-documented, but experts argue that the situation in the US wasn't predetermined. Senator Ron Wyden from Oregon has expressed his disappointment and frustration over the loss of measles-free status, labeling it a "tragic yet predictable outcome. A significant step taken by the government to combat the spread of measles is the allocation of $100 million to support state and local health departments in their response efforts. CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz reaffirmed the importance of vaccination in preventing measles transmission, stating that vaccination does" protect Americans from the disease. However, state and local health officials have pointed out that the cost of addressing this issue far exceeds the allocated funds, emphasizing the need for a stronger federal commitment to vaccinations. The lack of vocal support for vaccination efforts from high-ranking officials has been criticized by experts, who warn that inaction will only lead to more suffering. The lack of urgency from top officials has raised concerns among health experts as the US, Mexico, and Bolivia struggle to contain the measles outbreak. An inquiry about Kennedy's reaction to the US losing its measles-free status was met with a reference to Schwartz's statement by an HHS spokesperson. The best ski gear should be able to withstand long lift rides, changing weather patterns, and occasional tumbles without sacrificing fashion sense, it's not an either-or proposition. In fact, I firmly believe that style and functionality are intertwined, which is why Halfdays caught my attention three years ago and continues to keep me coming back season after season. Founded in 2020 by Olympic freestyle aerial skier Kiley McKinnon and Ariana Ferweda, Halfdays disrupted the ski apparel landscape with a refreshingly inclusive approach: creating women's gear that actually considers their needs. As I've accumulated a collection of ski and snowboard gear over the years, Halfdays' mission has resonated deeply with me - it's refreshing to see a brand that truly considers the needs of women in its designs. The brand's offerings have expanded significantly beyond just ski suits, bibs, and winter jackets, making it a one-stop shop for all my outdoor needs. From sweat-wicking baselayers to cozy fleeces and everyday essentials, Halfdays has proven itself to be a versatile player in the outdoor apparel market. One of the things I love about Halfdays is its ability to keep me comfortable and stylish even on the harshest winter days in New York City. Its knit headbands are perfect for covering my ears, while their winter leggings and warm socks strike just the right balance between warmth and thinness. The brand's evolution over time has been remarkable - what was once a ski-focused label has grown into a full-fledged outdoor brand with collections spanning hiking, running, and other warm-weather pursuits. This expansion is evident in its arrival at major retailers like Nordstrom and REI. Halfdays' collaborations have also helped cement its status as a go-to brand for outdoor enthusiasts - its recent team-up with Gigi Hadid's Guest in Residence on an eight-piece winter capsule is just one example of how the brand is pushing the boundaries of fashion and function. Halfdays' latest collaboration with Gore-Tex brings together the brand's signature mountainwear style with cutting-edge technical features, resulting in a collection that's both nostalgic and forward-thinking. The new line boasts an impressive array of high-performance outerwear, including down jackets, shells, bibs, and mittens, all designed to withstand even the harshest winter conditions. With Gore-Tex's renowned waterproof and breathable technology at its core, this collection is sure to be a game-changer for outdoor enthusiasts. As I gear up for another season of snow chasing, Halfdays' refreshing mix of style and substance continues to make it my go-to brand - and with this latest collaboration, it's clear that the brand is here to stay. articles.title: LIV Golf Players Face Uncertain Future Amid Bankruptcy Proceedings
articles.summary: The European tour has offered sponsor invitations to nine LIV Golf players, including major champions Dustin Johnson and Bubba Watson.
articles.content: The sudden collapse of LIV Golf has left its mark on the golf landscape, but it's now up to the governing bodies to find a solution for the affected players. As the dust settles on LIV Golf's bankruptcy proceedings, the focus shifts to the future of its players, who are suddenly more attractive than ever before. The speculation about which tours they would join has given way to a new question: who gets to return? The European tour has taken the initiative by offering sponsor invitations to nine players, provided they agree to a set number of appearances without requiring a hefty appearance fee. This move is likely to raise eyebrows among those who believe this concession undermines the tour's traditional revenue streams. This development highlights the complex web of interests at play in professional golf, where different tours and governing bodies have competing priorities. The European tour has taken a pragmatic approach, prioritizing its membership's interests above all else. Guy Kinnings, chief executive of the European tour, acknowledged that "there has been significant change in the landscape of men's professional golf over the past 12 months." He emphasized that his organization is taking a "pragmatic" stance to address this unprecedented situation. The European tour has been working on a plan to integrate players from the rival LIV league into their events. This move is aimed at revitalizing tournaments that are struggling to attract top talent due to depleted fields. Some of these LIV defectors have already secured spots on the European tour, leveraging their existing status earned through past performances. Bryson DeChambeau and Tyrrell Hatton are among those who have benefited from this arrangement, as have Paul Casey and David Puig. In a separate agreement, nine players will receive sponsor invitations to specific tournaments, with each player's deal varying in terms of the number of events they'll participate in. This list includes major champions Dustin Johnson, Bubba Watson, and Cameron Smith, as well as Joaquin Niemann. The European tour is eager to capitalize on this influx of talent, predicting that it will lead to a highly competitive 2027 season. According to Kinnings, the upcoming campaign will be one of the most closely contested in their 55-year history. As the PGA Tour's alliance with Europe nears its expiration date next year, both organizations are engaged in productive discussions about extending and modifying their partnership. This development is expected to have significant implications for players who have switched from LIV to the European tour. The number of PGA Tour cards that top European players will be eligible for is set to decrease as a result of this new development. Johnson's 24 tour wins have secured him lifetime membership on the PGA Tour, so he won't be affected by the change in card allocations. However, other high-profile players like Niemann, Ortiz, Ancer, and Herbert are likely to face difficulties in securing enough cards to continue competing at a top level. The uncertainty surrounding DeChambeau's playing schedule is another factor that has yet to be clarified, with his priority status as Europe's newest member not guaranteeing him a set number of tournament spots beyond the minimum required. Meanwhile, attention has turned to the players who have been left off the list of those receiving sponsor invitations, including some well-known names from LIV Golf. Players who were left off the list of those receiving sponsor invitations from LIV Golf are not without notable credentials. A significant number have won on the PGA Tour, a testament to their skill and experience. Among them is Caleb Surratt, a former NCAA champion who has also competed three times on the Challenge Tour. However, he was overlooked in favor of Michael La Sasso, another recent NCAA champion who recently took part in the final LIV event in Indianapolis. The decision to offer La Sasso an invitation instead of Surratt is seen as a footnote in history, particularly given that both players are still relatively young and at the height of their careers. articles.title: Nationwide Air Travel Shutdown Raises Questions About AI Role
articles.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has offered little clarity on the cause of last Friday's nationwide air travel shutdown, suggesting new AI software might be at fault.
articles.content: Reports of a nationwide air travel shutdown last Friday have left many wondering if AI was at fault. The Department of Homeland Security has offered little clarity on the matter, instead suggesting that new AI software might be to blame for the outage. In an interview with Fox News, Secretary Markwayne Mullin revealed that he's been told by someone "very smart with tech that the recent high-profile outages, including those at JPMorgan and Microsoft, could all be linked to the introduction of new AI systems. Mullin seemed uncertain about the claim, admitting that it kinda makes sense" but also leaving room for other possibilities. The complexity of modern infrastructure has been a pressing concern long before the advent of AI. Technologists have consistently highlighted the fragility and poor maintenance of America's digital and physical systems, which can lead to far-reaching consequences. These issues are not unique to any particular administration or ideology. Even with highly competent public servants in charge, the inherent complexity of these problems would persist. It is a challenge that requires a multifaceted approach, rather than simply assigning blame. The 2003 blackout serves as a stark reminder of this reality. A software glitch in Ohio led to widespread power outages across the country, including major cities like New York City. This incident demonstrates how seemingly isolated issues can have devastating effects on critical infrastructure. As AI continues to evolve and become increasingly integrated into these systems, concerns about its reliability and control are growing. Developers themselves often admit that they don't fully understand their creations or know how to manage them effectively. As we navigate the complexities of modern technology, it's becoming increasingly difficult to separate fact from fiction when it comes to outages and disruptions. One thing is certain: these events are happening more frequently, and with greater intensity. Whether it's a power grid failure or a social media meltdown, the impact on our daily lives is undeniable. Journalists like Josh Tyrangiel have likened our digital experience to living in Software Beirut, where anything can break at any time. This hyper-volatile environment makes it challenging for individuals to prepare for potential disruptions. For the average person, there's little that can be done to mitigate these risks. Stockpiling supplies, such as soup cans and water bottles, may seem like a futile effort, but it's a reminder of our vulnerability in the face of technological uncertainty. In contrast, members of the media have a responsibility to provide clarity and context during outages, asking tough questions and seeking answers from those responsible. The increasing number of outages has sparked debates about their causes, but one thing is clear: it's a challenging situation for all parties involved. To provide clarity during such times, it's essential to separate fact from fiction and avoid spreading misinformation. One simple yet effective way to do this is by remaining silent when faced with unverified information or hoaxes. A recent experience highlighted the importance of verifying information before sharing it with others. A social media post claiming a blackout on November 17 was brought up in an interview, but upon investigation, it turned out to be a made-up story with no basis in reality. To provide accurate and helpful responses to such queries, experts should be consulted and their findings shared with the public, rather than spreading unverified information that can cause more confusion.
