articles.title: Xbox Series X Owners Need to Check Their TV Ports for Optimal Performance
articles.summary: Gamers who plug their Xbox Series X into their TVs may not be getting the best picture quality due to outdated or incompatible ports.
articles.content: Many gamers who have invested in an Xbox Series X may not know that simply plugging the console into their television is not enough to unlock its full potential. While it's true that most modern TVs support high-definition standards like HDMI 2.1, not all of them are created equal - and neither are their ports. The key to getting the best out of your Xbox Series X lies in identifying which port on your TV actually supports this latest standard. The reason why this matters is because HDMI 2.1 is crucial for enjoying cutting-edge visual features like Variable Refresh Rate, a technology that smooths out framerate fluctuations and eliminates screen tearing. Without it, your Xbox Series X will be limited to lower resolutions and frame rates. If you own an older TV model that only supports HDMI 2.0, you're likely already aware of its limitations - but if you have a more recent budget-friendly flatscreen, there's a good chance that only one or two of its ports are compatible with the latest high-definition standard. When checking the HDMI ports on a modern TV, it's essential to know that not all of them may be compatible with the latest features. Most high-end sets released within the last two years have three to four HDMI 2.1 ports, but this is not always the case. Older TVs that support HDMI 2.1 may only have one or two compatible ports, while others may reserve these connections for specific slots. For instance, some Sony Bravia displays typically allocate their HDMI 2.1 configurations to ports three and four. To identify which HDMI ports on a TV are compatible with the Xbox Series X's 4K/120 max output, checking the model's online manual is recommended. Alternatively, individual inputs can be labeled on the backside of the TV itself, providing a clear indication of their capabilities. The labeling on some TVs can be misleading, as certain brands may prioritize HDMI 2.1 in specific slots. This means that even if a TV supports HDMI 2.1, not all its ports may be compatible with the latest features. Some premium OLED or MicroLED panels released within the last couple of years are likely to have all their HDMI inputs comply with HDMI 2.1 standards. However, it's crucial to verify this information for each individual model to avoid any potential issues. In some cases, TVs may reserve their best connections for specific ports, making it essential to check the manual or label on the backside of the TV to determine which ports are compatible with the Xbox Series X's requirements. When setting up your Xbox Series X, it's essential to ensure you're using the correct HDMI port on your TV. While most users won't need to replace the Ultra High Speed HDMI cable that comes in the box, there may be instances where a longer cable is necessary. The standard cable provided with the Xbox Series X is 6 feet long and should suffice for most gamers. However, if you have a large gaming setup or want more flexibility when placing your console, investing in a longer HDMI cable might be a good idea. Just make sure it's certified to support HDMI 2.1. For users who wall-mount their TVs, getting the Xbox Series X's HDMI cable into one of the TV's outputs can be challenging. In these cases, an ultra-thin connector on the HDMI cable can greatly simplify the process. It's crucial to verify that any new cable is also compliant with HDMI 2.1 standards. To avoid any potential issues, it's a good idea to check your TV's manual or label on the backside to determine which ports are compatible with the Xbox Series X's requirements. This will ensure a smooth gaming experience and prevent any connectivity problems down the line. The Xbox Series X is capable of impressive gaming performance, but its HDMI port configuration can sometimes get in the way. It's not uncommon for gamers to plug their console into the wrong HDMI port, which can lead to connectivity issues and a less-than-smooth gaming experience. Many games on the Xbox Series X are designed to run at high frame rates, with some titles even capable of hitting 120 frames per second. However, achieving this level of performance while also maintaining a 4K resolution is a challenge for many developers. Even popular first-party games like Indiana Jones and the Great Circle and Forza Horizon 6 can only manage 60 frames per second. When it comes to frame rates, some Xbox Series X games are more forgiving than others. Modern Call of Duty installments, such as Black Ops Cold War and Modern Warfare 4, are able to run at 120 frames per second, but often do so by deploying dynamic resolution techniques that can result in a lower in-game resolution. In most cases, achieving faster frame rates on the Xbox Series X requires accepting a dip in resolution. This is especially true for games like Doom the Dark Ages, which may not be able to maintain its native 4K resolution at high frame rates. The console's performance capabilities are often showcased through features like dynamic resolution scaling and improved texture filtering. These technologies help to ensure that games look their best on the Series X, even when running at higher frame rates. The visual quality of an Xbox Series X is heavily dependent on its connected display and HDMI cable. A high-quality HDMI 2.1 port and compatible cable are essential for delivering optimal performance and image clarity. When setting up your Xbox Series X, ensure that the console's HDMI ports and cables are properly configured to avoid any potential issues with visual output. articles.title: Guilty Verdict Handed Down to Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci
articles.summary: A court in The Hague has handed down another guilty verdict to former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci for obstructing justice and attempting to influence witnesses during his recent war crimes trial.
articles.content: A court in The Hague has handed down another guilty verdict to former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci, this time for obstructing justice and attempting to influence witnesses during his recent war crimes trial. The sentence of 17 months will be added to his existing 25-year term for war crimes. The charges stem from an indictment by the Specialist Prosecutor's Office, which alleges that Thaci shared confidential information about witnesses in his war crimes trial with visitors at a detention facility in The Hague. These individuals were reportedly instructed on how to influence the testimony of these witnesses. This is just the latest development in a complex and contentious case. Thaci has a complicated legacy in Kosovo, where he is viewed by many as a hero due to his role as the former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) during the 1998-1999 conflict. His war crimes conviction in September sparked widespread anger and dismay among his supporters back home. The conviction of three other men, former head of the Kosovo Intelligence Agency Bashkim Smakaj, former Minister of Justice Hajredin Kuci, and Fadil Fazliu, also raises questions about accountability. The Specialist Prosecutor's Office has been investigating allegations of war crimes committed during the 1998-1999 conflict in Kosovo. Thaci's actions, as described in the indictment, suggest a deliberate attempt to undermine the integrity of the trial process. His lawyers may argue that his intentions were not malicious, but rather an effort to protect himself from potential perjury charges. The conviction has sparked intense debate in Kosovo about the country's justice system and its ability to deliver fair verdicts. Kosovo society is grappling with complex emotions as it reflects on the war that ended 27 years ago, the role of former leaders, and the ongoing discussion about individual or collective responsibility for the KLA's actions during the conflict. The government responded swiftly to the ruling, issuing a statement that highlighted its commitment to upholding the rule of law. In a clear expression of its stance, the government emphasized that trust in justice is not solely built on the decisions made, but also on how those decisions are reached, stressing the importance of fair, transparent, and credible judicial processes. The appeal proceedings before the Kosovo Specialist Chambers have been a focal point for Kosovo's state authorities since Hashim Thaci's first conviction in September. To navigate this complex process, Kosovo has established a working group, led by Foreign Minister Glauk Konjufca, which includes members of the country's parliament. This initiative aims to develop a strategy for appealing the Specialist Chambers' decision at the appellate level. The government, under Prime Minister Albin Kurti, continues to express its dissatisfaction with the first-instance judgment, labeling it "unjust, both legally and morally". As a result, the authorities are working to secure a correction in the appeals process. Meanwhile, Kosovo's parliament is deliberating on amendments to the law governing the Specialist Chambers. These proposed changes aim to limit the court's jurisdiction in various areas, including the time frame of its authority and the maximum prison sentence allowed. The move by Kosovo's parliament to amend the law on the Specialist Chambers has sparked intense debate among analysts and experts about the country's commitment to justice. Political analyst Artan Muhaxheri believes that from an international perspective, the initiative could be seen as an attempt to interfere with the judicial process. He warns that if this is indeed the case, it would undermine Kosovo's efforts to demonstrate its ability to uphold the rule of law and adhere to its obligations towards the European Union. Muhaxheri emphasizes that for the amendment to be successful, it must be demonstrated that it does not conflict with Kosovo's international commitments. He stresses that this can only be achieved by ensuring that the proposed changes are argued professionally and rigorously, guaranteeing judicial independence and solidifying support within Kosovo's legal system. The Specialist Chambers were established by Kosovo itself, but their functioning has raised concerns about bias and prejudice in the justice process. Ehat Miftaraj, executive director of the Kosovo Law Institute (IKD), points out that judges, prosecutors, and international actors have sometimes treated accused individuals and the country as a whole with distrust, condescension, and an overly critical approach. Muhaxheri's advice to Kosovo's politicians is to carefully consider how their actions will be perceived internationally. He cautions that any move to undermine the Specialist Chambers could damage Kosovo's reputation and credibility on the world stage. The Specialist Chambers' decisions have sparked intense debate in Kosovo about justice and the role of the chambers themselves. Critics argue that reactions to these decisions are often rooted in a historical and emotional context that cannot be ignored. In this complex landscape, it's essential to distinguish between legitimate criticism of judicial decisions based on legal arguments and attempts to undermine the credibility of the courts or exert influence over their proceedings. The decision, he noted, lies squarely with the company's board of directors. Huang's departure as CEO came amidst allegations of personal misconduct, including an affair with a woman who is believed by U.S. intelligence officials to be a Chinese spy. Despite these revelations, Huang has stated that he would consider returning to his former position if the opportunity arises. Nadella and Huang have worked together for many years, and Nadella has acknowledged the significant impact Huang has had on Nvidia's success as well as the broader tech industry, particularly in the field of artificial intelligence chipmaking. Nvidia's success in the field of artificial intelligence has been a significant factor in the company's growth, and it's an area where they have made substantial investments. The partnership between Nvidia and Microsoft is also crucial to this effort, with the two companies working together on various projects. Microsoft has a long-standing relationship with Nvidia, which extends beyond their business dealings. In fact, interim CEO Colette Kress has a background at Microsoft, highlighting the talent pool available within the company. This depth of expertise will be essential in navigating the challenges ahead. The Vera Rubin line of processors is a key project for Nvidia and its partners, including Microsoft. The technology represents a significant step forward in processing power and efficiency, with potential applications across various industries. Scaling up production to meet demand will require close coordination between companies like Nvidia and Microsoft. As one of the world's leading cloud computing providers, Microsoft has a vested interest in Nvidia's success. Their partnership on projects such as the Vera Rubin line underscores their commitment to innovation and collaboration in the tech industry. Microsoft's Satya Nadella has emphasized that building data centers requires more than just lobbying in Washington or relying on public relations. He stressed that companies must physically demonstrate the benefits they bring to local communities and earn their support over time. Nadella acknowledged that communities often express concerns about data centers creating nuisances or driving up electricity bills, but he believes these fears are not entirely unfounded. In fact, he urged companies to take a long-term approach in addressing these issues and providing tangible value to the people they serve. The recent midterm elections have seen many communities reject AI data center development projects, with some even restricting data center construction altogether. However, Nadella's comments suggest that this outcome has not changed Microsoft's plans for building data centers, which are instead limited by factors such as power availability and supply chain constraints. A major disruption to Microsoft's systems last week affected millions of users worldwide, impacting services like Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and SharePoint. In a separate development, the company recently offered buyouts to nearly 30% of its workforce, around 60,000 employees, in an effort to streamline operations. Microsoft's Satya Nadella has clarified the cause of the recent outage, stating it was not due to AI code or deployments. Instead, he described it as a perfect storm" where a specific bug emerged under certain web traffic conditions during routine testing. This unexpected issue was actually mitigated by internal AI tools that helped engineers resolve the problem more efficiently. Nadella emphasized that the voluntary buyout offers were intended to give employees more control over their career paths, rather than leaving them uncertain about their job security. By offering a clear option, Nadella aimed to alleviate anxiety and provide a sense of agency for those considering their next steps. The move was not necessarily a precursor to layoffs. Nadella acknowledged that different teams within the company are progressing at varying speeds as part of its workplace transformation efforts. He noted that some teams are adapting more quickly than others, highlighting the complexity of this large-scale undertaking. articles.title: Google Replaces Gems with New Skills on Gemini Platform
articles.summary: Google is replacing an existing feature called Gems with something new: Skills, set to take place on November 17, 2026.
articles.content: Google has announced a significant change to its Gemini platform, where it is replacing an existing feature called Gems with something new: Skills. This shift is set to take place on November 17, 2026. The move involves carrying over features that allow users to share their creations and add files from various Google products into the new Skills format. Specifically, two key features from Gems are being transferred: the ability to share custom instructions with others, and the option to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files within those instructions. To facilitate a smooth transition for users, any Gems that have been created will automatically be converted into Skills. However, users can opt to manually transfer their Gems if they want to start using them before the changeover takes place. This manual transfer option is available now. Those who access the Gemini platform will notice a message informing them of the upcoming change: "Starting November 17, 2026, we'll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills." The way Gemini handles skills is similar to how it managed gems. Users describe specific situations where the skill should be applied and what action they want the skill to take. To make this clear, Google suggests providing examples of desired output. Unlike gems, which were standalone conversations, skills are custom instructions that can be used in any conversation. This makes them more versatile and easier to integrate into existing workflows. Skills have a limitation: only 100 can be active at a time. However, users are free to create as many skills as they need. To make the transition smoother, Google is bringing over two features from gems. One of these features allows users to share any skill with others. When sharing, users can choose whether to give the recipient permission to edit or view only. To access this feature, go to the three-bar menu in the top left and select Customize > Skills. Users can choose to have Gemini use a newly added Skill automatically or manually trigger it in chat by mentioning its name preceded by the @ symbol. For now, Skills can only be shared through the web app of Google's conversational AI tool, with mobile app users unable to access this feature yet. When creating a new Skill, users can include files from other Google services like Drive and Photos, as well as local device files, up to 100MB in size. articles.title: Altria Group's CEO Discusses Challenges in Nicotine Business
articles.summary: Altria's On! nicotine pouch brand is struggling to compete with Philip Morris's Zyn due to regulatory hurdles and a misconception about nicotine's harm.
articles.content: Altria Group's CEO Sal Mancuso emphasized the importance of responsibility in the company's FDA-regulated nicotine business during a recent forum in Detroit. The shift towards less harmful nicotine alternatives by Big Tobacco companies has created new challenges for their relationships with regulators, particularly when it comes to competing with other businesses in the space. Altria's On! nicotine pouch brand is a key innovation for the company, but regulations have slowed growth, making it harder for the company to compete. The Marlboro-maker announced its Moving Beyond Smoking initiative last year as consumers increasingly turn away from cigarettes and towards smoke-free alternatives like NJOY vapes and On! nicotine pouches. Altria's focus on these products has led to a renewed emphasis on competing with Philip Morris's Zyn in the market. Altria's CEO Sal Mancuso acknowledged that the company is currently at a disadvantage in the pouch category, but expressed confidence in its ability to lead the way over time. According to Mancuso, one of the main obstacles facing the industry is the widespread misconception that nicotine itself causes harm from tobacco use. Mancuso also highlighted the challenges posed by FDA regulations on his company's business, stating that responsibility must be at the forefront of everything Altria does in the nicotine sector. This emphasis on responsibility reflects the changing landscape of the tobacco industry and its growing focus on smoke-free products. Altria's lawsuit against the FDA is centered on the regulatory agency's review process for new tobacco products. The company claims that this process has become a major hurdle in getting its newer nicotine products to market. Specifically, Altria alleges that the FDA's evaluation of these products takes significantly longer than the 180-day deadline set by law. The Premarket Tobacco Product Application (PMTA) review process is a key point of contention between Altria and the FDA. Under this process, new tobacco products must undergo a thorough examination to determine whether they provide an overall public health benefit. However, Altria argues that the FDA's bureaucratic red tape has led to excessively long delays in reviewing these applications. Meanwhile, foreign competitors are flooding store shelves with their own nicotine products, often mislabeled as being made in the US. This not only erodes market share for legitimate companies but also allows illicit products to circumvent safety standards set by the FDA. Altria claims that this is a major concern and that enforcement against these illegal products is urgently needed. The issue of labeling is particularly problematic, with overseas products being marketed as made in the US when they are actually imported from countries like China. This misrepresentation can lead consumers to believe that these products meet stricter safety standards than they actually do. The FDA's failure to address this issue has created a regulatory vacuum that Altria is seeking to fill through its lawsuit. As part of its efforts to overhaul the PMTA review process, Altria is pushing for revisions to be made by the FDA. This includes streamlining the application process and reducing the time it takes for products to reach market. By doing so, Altria hopes to create a more level playing field for legitimate companies and reduce the proliferation of illicit nicotine products. The regulatory framework governing nicotine products is in dire need of reform, according to Altria's CEO, who believes that excessive information and lack of durability in guidelines hinder legitimate businesses from operating effectively. A more streamlined approach to regulation would allow companies like Altria to focus on delivering high-quality products while providing consumers with a wider range of choices. Rapid authorization processes would enable consumers to access various nicotine products without unnecessary delays or uncertainty. The regulatory landscape for cannabis in the US, where half of states have legalized it but lack federal standards, serves as a relevant example. This "hodgepodge" of regulations creates an uneven playing field that favors illicit operators over responsible businesses like Altria.
